title: Hertzian dipole at 10 GHz at the centre of a 30 mm sphere whose outer 15 mm shell is a spherical perfectly matched layer: radiated power and directivity
source: The Hertzian dipole of moment I·l = 1 mA·m in free space: P = η (k I l)²/(12π), directivity D(θ) = (3/2) sin²θ from its axis (C. A. Balanis, Antenna Theory, 4th ed., Wiley 2016, §4.2, eqs. 4-16, 4-31), evaluated separately (η = μ₀c)

quantities.reason: through a Huygens sphere of 10 mm radius, 5 mm inside the layer; second-order elements of λ/8 and a layer of half a wavelength: +0.8 %. At this size the error is the source's: the current element is spread over the tetrahedron holding it, whose size and shape move the power by +0.8 to +2.4 % over three placements within 0.4 mm of the centre (the layer's design reflection, 1e-3 to 1e-9, by under 1 %; a Huygens box in place of the sphere gives the same)
the near-to-far transform of the Huygens sphere's currents, 3 Gauss points on bands of λ/12 in θ and 3 points per λ/12 in φ: +1.2 % (−0.2 to +1.2 % over the three placements)

quantities.quantity: directivity at θ = 20° (near the null on the axis)
quantities.reason: a weak field near the axis, where the source element's higher multipoles weigh most: −3.1 % (−2.2 to −5.9 %)
